newsitem.title: BRAZIL: U.S. slaps ban on firearms exports to Paraguay.
newsitem.headline: U.S. slaps ban on firearms exports to Paraguay.

text.p: The United States has banned arms sales to Paraguay to stem the flow of contraband weapons reaching criminals in neighbouring Brazil and other countries, the U.S. Embasssy in Brazil said on Wednesday.
"The U.S. State Department has suspended all licenses for the export of firearms, rifles, components and ammunition to Paraguay," the embassy said in a statement.
Only some hunting rifles will be exempt from the ban and their sales will be closely monitored by the Commerce Department.
The ban was taken "in response to concerns regarding the illegal flow of weapons from Paraguay to other countries," the statement said.

"The U.S. government, on reviewing its export licenses, concluded that firearms which are legally exported from the United States cross Paraguayan borders illegally, supplying criminals in Brazil," it said.

The State Department revoked all existing arms export licenses for Paraguay on Monday and banned new licenses until the Paraguayan government develops a system to stop weapons smuggling that meets with U.S. norms, the statement said.
Authorities in Brazil say the smuggling of weapons into the country increased 26 percent over the past year, with most of them coming from Paraguay.

In a bid to address rising violence in Brazil, the lower house of Congress earlier this month approved a bill mandating jail sentences for carriers of unlicensed weapons. The bill now faces a vote in the Senate.
